audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 was marked Skill in both layers while the page's own whys[2] says he wins the extended trade there, and the packet chart gives level 3 to Darius. The phase whys for levels 1, 2 and 3 were boilerplate that claimed Gragas wins level 1 outright while the side field said Darius.
audit.why: Pre-6 Gragas has no answer to Apprehend into the Decimate blade: Hemorrhage ticks through the trade and Happy Hour only procs on cast, so the first four stages belong to Darius.
audit.corrected: Level 3 flipped to Darius in both layers with the rating dropped, and the level 1/2/3/first-item whys rewritten to state the actual reason each stage is his.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item phase claimed Riftmaker as a Gragas spike to 'force fights the moment it completes' while its side field says Darius.
audit.why: Riftmaker sustain narrows the gap but does not beat a Stridebreaker re-engage; who starts the fight is still decided by Apprehend, which is 26s at rank 1 and 16s at rank 5 — the single most punishable cooldown in the lane.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why now keys the window to Apprehend's 26s rather than promising a Gragas spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block and trade lines were generic ('your committal tool', 'his key tool') and never gave Apprehend's 26s, Body Slam's 14s or Explosive Cask's 100s, and never stated that Body Slam is your escape from the pull rather than your engage.
audit.why: Apprehend at 26s rank 1 is a two-and-a-half-Body-Slam window; naming it makes the hold-E-to-escape rule concrete. Explosive Cask's knockback is the tool that resets his Hemorrhage pressure before five stacks enrage him and fuel a resetting Noxian Guillotine.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block, tradeGood, tradeBad and the long-fight don't now carry the real numbers and the bleed-stack consequence.

audit.why: The flagged suspectName "Barrel Roll's" is a false positive — Barrel Roll is the real name of Gragas's Q.

edits.before: Q-poke from range wins level 1 outright. Identify how Darius contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: No Happy Hour proc until you cast, and his Apprehend pull plus Hemorrhage wins the level-1 trade outright.

edits.before: W damage reduction + sustain flips his return trade. Only take the trade when Darius's Apprehend is down.
edits.after: His empowered Decimate off a pull out-damages your Barrel Roll, and you cannot sustain the bleed yet.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Darius must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Stuck between long cooldowns without your full combo, you lose the extended trade his bleed and Decimate are built to win.

edits.before: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Apprehend's cooldown.
edits.after: Riftmaker sustain helps, but Apprehend at 26s rank 1 still decides who starts the fight.

edits.before: - Darius Apprehend: matchup-defining — His all-in starts on the pull. E away from it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Darius Apprehend: 26s at rank 1 — his all-in starts on the pull, so hold Body Slam to escape it, not to engage. - Your Body Slam: 14s. - Explosive Cask: 100s — knock him off you before five bleed stacks land.

edits.before: Q-poke Darius on cooldown from fog angles, W as he answers, and E-slam only when his key tool is down.
edits.after: Q-poke Darius from fog angles, W as he answers, and E-slam only in the window after Apprehend whiffs.

edits.before: Body-slamming INTO his answer — a whiffed E is 13 seconds of being a barrel with no plan.
edits.after: Body-slamming into his pull range — a whiffed E is 14 seconds with no escape from Apprehend.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Five bleed stacks enrage him and fuel a resetting Guillotine.
